tools.name: mailboxes_list
tools.title: List mailboxes
tools.description: List the connected mailboxes that answer - Gmail, Outlook.com and Hotmail, Microsoft 365 and any other email account read over IMAP - each by the name a tool's mailbox input takes, with its service, whether it is a personal or a work account, the search language it reads, whether it needs reconnecting, the tools its provider does not offer and those the person turned off, and its inbox's counts. It counts no action.

tools.name: messages_list
tools.title: Search a mailbox
tools.description: Search one connected mailbox in its own provider's query language, Gmail's or Outlook's, narrowed by the inputs beside q, or list its mail by those inputs alone. An Outlook mailbox without q reads one folder, the inbox unless folder names another, in order; with q it searches every folder and leaves off each page what the other inputs rule out, filtered counting them, so a short page can have more after it, and it answers no match past its 1,000th, ceiling marking the page where it stopped. Any other mailbox whose provider is imap leaves off each page what an instant, a size or has:attachment rules out, filtered counting them, and names under notSearched each folder the call had no time left to search. A message whose recipients one answer cannot carry names the first that fit, omittedRecipients counting the rest. The times it answers with carry their offset in the person's own time zone, which the answer names under now beside their time now in it - UTC where the person has stored no zone, as now says.

mailbox.description: The mailbox's name or its email address.

q.description: A Gmail mailbox, whatever its provider, reads Gmail's search operators: from:, to:, cc:, subject:, is:unread, is:starred, in:sent, has:attachment, filename:pdf, after:2026/01/31, before:, newer_than:7d, larger:5M, OR, -word and ( ). An Outlook mailbox reads Microsoft's keyword query language - from:, to:, cc:, subject:, body:, received:, hasAttachments:true, plain words and quoted phrases, AND, OR and NOT in capitals - and never a filter expression such as isRead eq false. A few distinctive words, with OR between alternatives, miss less than a copied subject line or sentence. Any other mailbox whose provider is imap reads only from:, to: and cc: (never me), subject:, plain words and quoted phrases, -word or -"a phrase" leaving it out, is:unread, one run of OR between any of those (as a OR b OR c), has:attachment, and larger: and smaller: in bytes or as 500K or 5M, after: and before: as 2026/01/31, newer_than: in days, months or years, and one in: or label: naming one folder, by the name labels_list gives a label of type user or as inbox, sent, archive, drafts, spam or trash, a name holding a space quoted and a quote or backslash inside the quotes taking a backslash before it, with no AND or NOT, and is searched by message in every folder but the bin and junk. after: and before: written as a bare date open at midnight in the person's own time zone, save in an Outlook mailbox's query, whose dates Microsoft reads itself.

unread.description: true answers unread mail alone, false read mail alone.

flagged.description: true answers flagged mail alone - starred on Gmail, flagged on Outlook - false the rest.

folder.description: One folder to search: inbox, sent, archive, drafts, deleted or junk, or a folder's id from labels_list - on a Gmail connected by Google sign-in any label's, on Outlook a folder's and never a category's. A mailbox whose provider is imap takes no folder in q beside it.

focus.description: Outlook alone: focused answers the mail Outlook sorts into Focused, other the mail in Other. Outlook sorts its inbox alone, and reads mail in every other folder as focused.

after.description: Only mail that arrived at or after this instant, with its offset, as 2026-10-20T00:00:00Z.

before.description: Only mail that arrived before this instant, written and read as after is.

order.description: newest, the default, answers the newest mail first; oldest the oldest. Gmail answers newest first alone, and so does Outlook with q.

by.description: message, the default, answers each matching message; thread answers each matching thread with every message in it.

view.description: summary, the default, carries each message's subject and snippet; headers leaves both out; compact, the lightest page, carries only each message's id, threadId, sender, date, unread mark, subject and the first 100 characters of its snippet.

maxResults.description: How many results to take, 10 where left out.

pageToken.description: The nextPageToken of the page before, asked with every other input the same. Outlook, and a Gmail whose provider is imap, page threads by their matching messages, so a thread can recur on a later page.

tools.name: messages_list_all_mailboxes
tools.title: Search every mailbox
tools.description: Search every mailbox you have connected - every email account at once - in one call, or only those mailboxes names. The answer names the mailbox each result came from, names any mailbox it could not search, and is merged newest first by when each message arrived, a thread by its newest. A message whose recipients one answer cannot carry names the first that fit, omittedRecipients counting the rest. One search for what arrived after: the time of the last look is the cheapest way to watch for new mail. The times it answers with carry their offset in the person's own time zone, which the answer names under now beside their time now in it - UTC where the person has stored no zone, as now says.

q.description: A Gmail mailbox, whatever its provider, reads Gmail's search operators: from:, to:, cc:, subject:, is:unread, is:starred, in:sent, has:attachment, filename:pdf, after:2026/01/31, before:, newer_than:7d, larger:5M, OR, -word and ( ). An Outlook mailbox reads Microsoft's keyword query language - from:, to:, cc:, subject:, body:, received:, hasAttachments:true, plain words and quoted phrases, AND, OR and NOT in capitals - and never a filter expression such as isRead eq false. A few distinctive words, with OR between alternatives, miss less than a copied subject line or sentence. Any other mailbox whose provider is imap reads only from:, to: and cc: (never me), subject:, plain words and quoted phrases, -word or -"a phrase" leaving it out, is:unread, one run of OR between any of those (as a OR b OR c), has:attachment, and larger: and smaller: in bytes or as 500K or 5M, after: and before: as 2026/01/31, newer_than: in days, months or years, and one in: or label: naming one folder, by the name labels_list gives a label of type user or as inbox, sent, archive, drafts, spam or trash, a name holding a space quoted and a quote or backslash inside the quotes taking a backslash before it, with no AND or NOT, and is searched by message in every folder but the bin and junk. Every mailbox is asked these alike, in its own provider's language or applied to what it answers: from:, to: and cc: (never me), subject:, plain words and quoted phrases, OR between any of those (as a OR b OR c), -word or -"a phrase" leaving it out, is:unread, has:attachment, larger: in bytes or as 500K or 5M, in:trash or in:spam searching the bin or spam alone, and dates: after: and before: as 2026/01/31, read as midnight in the time zone answers name under now, or with an offset as 2026-01-31T09:00+01:00, and newer_than: as 7d, 2m or 1y, each mailbox answering only what arrived inside the period, with no AND, NOT, AROUND, NEAR or ONEAR in capitals. A password mailbox other than a Gmail reads one run of OR, and a query holding more leaves it out. Where the mailboxes read different languages - a Gmail reads Gmail's, whatever its provider - a query holding any other term is refused; where they read one, it is asked whole. Left out, every message is answered.

by.description: message, the default, answers each matching message; thread answers each matching thread with every message in it.

view.description: summary, the default, carries each message's subject and snippet; headers leaves both out; compact, the lightest page, carries only each message's id, threadId, sender, date, unread mark, subject and the first 100 characters of its snippet.

mailboxes.description: The mailboxes to search, each by its name or email address; every one where none is named.

items.description: The mailbox's name or its email address.

pageToken.description: The nextPageToken of the answer before, asked with every other input the same: it searches on each mailbox it names from where that mailbox's page stopped, and no other. A thread can recur on a later page.

waiting.description: on_me answers only the threads waiting for the person's reply - their newest message someone else's, addressed to them; on_others only those waiting on another's - their newest message the person's own. Every mailbox is then read by thread, whatever by says, and each thread is answered with its newest message alone, drafts aside; one whose newest message reports a failed delivery is marked bounced and waits on nobody. A thread is picked by who wrote last and to whom - on any other mailbox whose provider is imap, by its answered mark - never by what its message asks, which its words alone say. A page holds only what waits, so it can be short while more names a mailbox holding more. A Gmail, whatever its provider, and an Outlook mailbox answer both; any other mailbox whose provider is imap answers on_me by the mail no mail app marked answered and cannot answer on_others.

run.description: The name of a task this search is one run of, repeated as on a schedule - 1 to 40 letters, digits and hyphens. Each mailbox is then read from ten minutes before the last run under that name began reading it, or for the last 24 hours where none has, its first run, as its asked entry says under run. A mailbox's mark moves only once a run answers its whole period to its last page, so one not reached or not paged to its end is read from its older mark next time, and nextPageToken under the same run pages on to it. An account keeps 50 names, the longest unused forgotten first.

tools.name: drafts_create
tools.title: Draft a message
tools.description: Compose an email in a connected mailbox and keep it there as a draft. An address the person did not give is found in their past mail - messages_list_all_mailboxes with from: or to: and the name, at the headers view - and is theirs to confirm before anything is written to it. The person's own last letter to someone - the newest found with to: and their address whose sender is an address mailboxes_list names - shows the manner they write to them in. Where the address it goes from has a signature - settings_send_as_get reads the default address's - the signature goes below your words and above any quote, so a sign-off, name, title, phone number or link in the words repeats it, and sign false leaves it off a terse note; where it has none, the words close as the person's own would.

mailbox.description: The mailbox's name or its email address.

to.description: Who the message is addressed to. A draft may name nobody yet; it is sent only once it names someone.

bcc.description: Who to blind-copy. The other recipients are not told.

body.description: The message text; html alone is enough, its text read from it.

html.description: The message as HTML, for formatting; body stays its plain-text version, read from it where left out. An Outlook mailbox keeps only the HTML and writes the plain version from it.

A file you hold and can send yourself by HTTP PUT, as from a terminal, is named by filename and mimeType alone: the call then writes nothing and answers with an address to put it at, and the same call made again names it by the upload that answer gave it. Any other file is written out, kept small.

On Gmail a new subject moves the draft out of its conversation into one of its own; on Outlook the answer names the conversation the draft is kept in. A mailbox whose provider is imap keeps the edited draft under a new id the answer names, and the old id then reads nothing; an old version its server did not remove stays in Drafts, named as previousVersionId. An address the person did not give is found in their past mail - messages_list_all_mailboxes with from: or to: and the name, at the headers view - and is theirs to confirm before anything is written to it. The person's own last letter to someone - the newest found with to: and their address whose sender is an address mailboxes_list names - shows the manner they write to them in.

body.description: Your own words. Any other file is written out, kept small. Named, they replace the ones it holds - never the pictures inside its words - and an empty list removes them all. Where the address it goes from has a signature - settings_send_as_get reads the default address's - the signature goes below your words and above any quote, so a sign-off, name, title, phone number or link in the words repeats it, and sign false leaves it off a terse note; where it has none, the words close as the person's own would.

tools.name: labels_list
tools.title: List labels
tools.description: List the labels a connected mailbox holds, by the id each is applied by. A mailbox whose provider is imap holds its folders as labels, nested by /, beside UNREAD, STARRED and SPAM. An Outlook mailbox's labels are its categories, of type category, and its own folders, of type folder, each named by its path with how many messages it holds and how many are unread; Outlook's own folders - the inbox, sent mail, drafts, Deleted Items, Junk and the like - are not labels. A Gmail connected by Google sign-in also holds Gmail's own labels, of type system, among them IMPORTANT, Gmail's mark of what matters, and its inbox tabs as CATEGORY_PERSONAL, CATEGORY_SOCIAL, CATEGORY_PROMOTIONS, CATEGORY_UPDATES and CATEGORY_FORUMS, which threads_modify applies and removes as it does the person's own.

tools.name: labels_create
tools.title: Create a label
tools.description: Create a label in a connected mailbox and answer the id it is applied by. In a Gmail mailbox, and as a folder in one whose provider is imap or in an Outlook mailbox, a / nests it under the label before it, made first where missing. An Outlook mailbox makes a folder where the name holds a / or folder is true, and a category otherwise.

mailbox.description: The mailbox's name or its email address.

folder.description: In an Outlook mailbox, true makes a folder rather than a category.

tools.name: labels_update
tools.title: Edit a label
tools.description: Rename a label, recolour it, or both. The id comes from labels_list. A new name carries the labels nested under it by / with it. An Outlook mailbox's category takes only a new colour, as Microsoft allows, and its folder only a new name, given where it is and keeping its id. A mailbox whose provider is imap renames its folder, which takes no colour, and answers the label's new id.

mailbox.description: The mailbox's name or its email address.

tools.name: labels_delete
tools.title: Delete a label
tools.description: Delete one label, by its id from labels_list. No message is deleted: in a Gmail connected by Google sign-in the label comes off every message; an Outlook mailbox's category leaves its list, and the messages that carried it keep its name. A mailbox whose provider is imap, a Gmail one included, deletes only a folder holding no mail and no folder, and so does an Outlook mailbox.

mailbox.description: The mailbox's name or its email address.

tools.name: threads_modify
tools.title: Label a thread
tools.description: Apply and remove labels on one thread, or one message of it, to file it in a folder, star it or mark it read or unread - an Outlook mailbox's categories and its own folders are its labels. The ids come from labels_list. Adding STARRED to a thread stars its newest message the person received - on an Outlook mailbox, flags it - as their own mail app does, and removing it unstars every message. Adding SPAM junks it, and taking SPAM off brings it back to the inbox. Adding INBOX brings it back from the archive. In a Gmail connected by Google sign-in adding TRASH bins it too; an Outlook mailbox takes UNREAD, STARRED, SPAM and INBOX beside its categories and its folders, and no other id, and junks a thread's inbox messages alone, filing into one folder a call: adding a folder moves the messages into it from whatever folder each is in, and a folder is left only for another folder added - never Deleted Items, Junk or a folder under either, which threads_trash and SPAM own - or for INBOX, which brings them back; a Gmail mailbox whose provider is imap takes only UNREAD, STARRED, SPAM, INBOX and its own labels, several a call, as Gmail does, each message keeping its id; any other mailbox whose provider is imap takes only UNREAD, STARRED, SPAM, INBOX and its folders' labels, filing into one folder a call: adding a label moves the messages into its folder from whatever folder each is in - so removing one label and adding another moves them from one folder to the other - and removing labels alone moves their messages back to the inbox, each message moved taking a new id, which the answer names. There, and in an Outlook mailbox, a thread's sent mail and drafts, and any message in the provider's own scheduled, snoozed or outgoing folder - in an Outlook mailbox its copies of mail it could not sync too - stay where they are, untouched, each answered with skipped saying which. Outlook and a mailbox whose provider is imap take INBOX added, never removed - threads_archive takes a thread out of the inbox - and move nothing out of the bin, which is threads_untrash's: outside a Gmail, a binned message they would have moved is answered with skipped. With ids in place of id it takes 2 to 100 at once under one call's time, counted as one action: each thread it reached is answered under threads - done; notDone, saying why; or possiblyDone, moved in part or asked with no answer back, which threads_get - or messages_get for a message - reads to check - and each it did not reach, its time spent, its connection lost or the mailbox refusing it whole, is left untouched under notReached, for the same call again.

It stays in the mailbox and in search. Any other mailbox whose provider is imap moves its inbox messages into its archive folder, made as Archive where it has none, each under a new id the answer names. With ids in place of id it takes 2 to 100 at once under one call's time, counted as one action: each thread it reached is answered under threads - done; notDone, saying why; or possiblyDone, moved in part or asked with no answer back, which threads_get - or messages_get for a message - reads to check - and each it did not reach, its time spent, its connection lost or the mailbox refusing it whole, is left untouched under notReached, for the same call again.

A Gmail mailbox whose provider is imap keeps every label but the inbox on it and each message its id; in any other mailbox whose provider is imap each moved message takes a new id, which the answer names. With ids in place of id it takes 2 to 100 at once under one call's time, counted as one action: each thread it reached is answered under threads - done; notDone, saying why; or possiblyDone, moved in part or asked with no answer back, which threads_get - or messages_get for a message - reads to check - and each it did not reach, its time spent, its connection lost or the mailbox refusing it whole, is left untouched under notReached, for the same call again.

A Gmail mailbox whose provider is imap puts a draft back in its drafts, the owner's own mail in sent mail and the rest in the inbox, with every label it carried, each message keeping its id. An Outlook mailbox and any other mailbox whose provider is imap put a message threads_trash moved there back in the folder that move took it from - the latest such move, within 30 days, while that folder is still there outside the trash - and any other message by that same rule; each message they bring back names the folder it went to as restoredTo, and in a mailbox whose provider is imap the new id it took. tools.name: messages_attachments_get
tools.title: Read an attachment
tools.description: Read one attachment of a message. The answer is what it says, as plain text; with as original it is the file itself, base64, or a picture too large for one answer shrunk to fit. messages_get and threads_get name a message's attachments and their sizes. Either answer names a link the original is served at whole for 15 minutes after it is given, to a plain GET carrying no credential. From a terminal, curl --fail-with-body -o <a new path of your own> "<link>" fetches it; a refused fetch exits non-zero and leaves its reason in that file.

mailbox.description: The mailbox's name or its email address.

messageId.description: The message's id, as a search or a read answered it.

id.description: An attachment id, as a message read named it.

as.description: text, the default: what the file says. original: the file itself, byte for byte, or a picture too large for one answer shrunk to fit.

continuation.description: Where the words resume, as the last part read named it. The original always comes whole.

tools.name: sweeps_preview
tools.title: Preview a clear-out
tools.description: Count who fills one folder of a mailbox, the inbox unless folder names another, before clearing it out by sender - newsletters, promotions and notifications a group at a time rather than thread by thread, each group sweeps_apply moves once the person approves it; nothing is moved. The answer numbers the 20 senders with the most mail there, each with its count, how many are unread, its newest and oldest dates, two of its subjects, and heldApart: how many are receipts, orders, bookings, bills, account or security notices. otherSenders and otherMessages count the rest, and nextSenders names the next 20 of them by address with how many messages each has, for another preview to name in senders. A sender whose name screens as a prompt attack is withheld with its group, which takes no number, counted under withheldSenders and withheldMessages; a subject that does leaves its group's subjects, counted under withheldSubjects; a next sender's address that does leaves nextSenders, counted under withheldNextSenders. Flagged mail, drafts, the person's own messages, mail from people they write to, and everything in sent, drafts, deleted or junk is in no group, counted under leftOut instead. At most the newest 10,000 messages of an Outlook folder, or of a mailbox held by its password, are read, and notReadBefore names the date before which a larger folder was not. A mailbox held by its password is cleared out only where its mail server names where it moves each message, and a Gmail held by its password out of its inbox alone. Gmail allows few reads a minute, so only the newest 150 of a Gmail folder are read: they choose the groups, and each group's messages then counts all its sender's mail the preview asks for, up to 10,000 in all, unless the preview narrows by subject; its other figures, otherSenders, otherMessages, nextSenders and leftOut count the messages read, and folderTotal is Gmail's own estimate. actionsLeft is how many actions this account has left in its daily allowance after this call. sweep is the handle sweeps_apply clears what was counted by, held an hour; what an apply moves can be put back until putBackUntil at the earliest. The times it answers with carry their offset in the person's own time zone, which the answer names under now beside their time now in it - UTC where the person has stored no zone, as now says.

mailbox.description: The mailbox's name or its email address.

folder.description: The folder to read, inbox by default; all of sent, drafts, deleted and junk is left out.

senders.description: Only mail from these addresses is counted.

domain.description: Only mail from this domain or one under it is counted, as example.com.

subject.description: Only mail whose subject holds this phrase, letter case aside, is counted.

excludeSubjects.description: Mail whose subject holds any of these phrases is left out of the count.

olderThanDays.description: Only mail that arrived more than this many days ago is counted.

unread.description: true counts only unread mail, false only read mail.

keepNewest.description: The newest this many of each sender's messages are left out of the count, so only the rest is counted.

focus.description: Outlook alone: only the mail Outlook sorts into Focused, or only that in Other, is counted. Outlook sorts its inbox alone.

tab.description: Gmail alone: only the mail in this tab of its inbox is counted, as focus counts Outlook's Focused or Other.

list.description: Only mail from this mailing list is counted, by its list id: what a message's listId holds between its angle brackets, as news.example.com.

largerThanBytes.description: Only mail larger than this many bytes is counted, as 5000000 for mail over 5 MB.

tools.name: sweeps_apply
tools.title: Clear out a preview
tools.description: Move the groups a sweeps_preview counted, each to the trash - Deleted Items in Outlook - or the archive, or into a label or folder the person made in that mailbox, named by its id from labels_list, or mark a group's unread mail read where it is; Gmail moves mail by its labels, taking the inbox label off and adding Trash or the label filed into, and a mailbox held by its password into its trash, archive or label folder - a Gmail's archive being All Mail. Filing into the inbox, the bin, junk, sent mail, drafts, the archive, a Gmail tab or another label Gmail keeps itself is refused (file_refused). Each group is named by its number with the messages count the preview answered, and any count that differs refuses the whole call. Left-out mail is a group too, archived, filed or marked read, never binned: flagged 21, drafts 22, sent 23, own 24, writtenTo 25; deleted and junk mail is never moved. Binning needs a preview narrowed by senders, a domain, a subject phrase or olderThanDays of 30 or more, and leaves a group's receipts, orders, bookings, bills, account and security notices where they are (heldApart). Marking read leaves mail already read as it is (alreadyRead), so putting back never marks it unread. A message changed since the preview is left where it is. A call works for about three minutes and answers per group what moved or was marked read, what changed and what it did not reach, which stays untouched, with up to 20 failures. The same call again under the same sweep, while anything is notReached or failed as unavailable, carries on where the last stopped, settles any message a call cut short left mid-move, and counts no action against the daily allowance. sweeps_put_back puts it back until putBackUntil. The times it answers with carry their offset in the person's own time zone, which the answer names under now beside their time now in it - UTC where the person has stored no zone, as now says.

mailbox.description: The mailbox's name or its email address.

messages.description: The group's count, as the preview answered it.

label.description: For file alone: the id labels_list gives the label or folder the group goes into.

onlyIfNewest.description: true acts only while this sweep's preview is still the newest of its mailbox, refused (sweep_replaced) once a newer one is held.

tools.name: sweeps_put_back
tools.title: Put a clear-out back
tools.description: Return what sweeps_apply moved under a sweep handle - every group, or those named - each message to the Outlook folder, or the folder of a mailbox held by its password, it came from, or in Gmail connected by Google sign-in to the labels it held; mail it marked read is marked unread again, and only that, and mail it filed leaves the label or folder, a label it already carried staying on it. A message moved since the apply is left where it is (changed), and one the provider no longer holds is gone. A call works for about three minutes; the same call again reaches what it did not. Putting back counts no action against the daily allowance.

tools.name: settings_filters_list
tools.title: List filters
tools.description: List the rules a connected mailbox files incoming mail by, each marked where it forwards, redirects, bins, junks, deletes or hides mail, whoever made it, with the folders it files into and when the person's AI clients made it; an Outlook mailbox's list also names each sender it always sorts into Focused or Other, by placement; and a Gmail mailbox's list, unlike an Outlook one's, also says whether Gmail forwards all its mail, and where.

mailbox.description: The mailbox's name or its email address.

tools.name: settings_filters_create
tools.title: Create a filter
tools.description: Create a rule - a filter - that files a connected mailbox's incoming mail from now on: out of the inbox, under a label, into a folder or marked read. A rule that carries mail out of the mailbox, or that bins or junks what it matches, is refused, whether or not the provider would take it. A rule matches mail meeting every condition it names, and on an Outlook mailbox leaves alone mail meeting any one under except; a condition or action the mailbox's provider cannot hold is refused there, never approximated. An Outlook mailbox's rule files under its categories (addLabelIds), into one folder (folder), out of the inbox (removeLabelIds INBOX), as read (removeLabelIds UNREAD) and at an importance (markImportance); a Gmail mailbox's folder is a label it files under out of the inbox. Senders are blocked by one rule from them with addLabelIds a label named Blocked - made with labels_create where labels_list holds none, on an Outlook mailbox a category - removeLabelIds ["INBOX", "UNREAD"], and on an Outlook mailbox stop true; muted by removeLabelIds ["UNREAD"] alone. Neither deletes anything. What no rule can hold - by age, the newest few from each sender, first-time senders or by meaning - is a clear-out instead: sweeps_preview takes olderThanDays and keepNewest, and the ready request Keep my inbox tidy, offered to the person, sets one up as a scheduled task. On an Outlook mailbox, focus with from alone puts those senders always in Focused or always in Other instead of making a rule.

tools.name: settings_filters_update
tools.title: Change a filter
tools.description: Change one rule by its id from settings_filters_list, naming its conditions and actions whole as settings_filters_create takes them - its sender list included - or, on an Outlook mailbox, pause or resume it with enabled. A change replaces every condition, exception and action the rule holds, so anything settings_filters_list shows of it that this tool cannot name is dropped - a loss the person agrees to first. A change is refused wherever a new rule would be. A rule marked as forwarding, redirecting, binning, junking or deleting mail is only paused or removed from here, and one Outlook marks read-only is not changed at all. Outlook keeps the rule's id; Gmail changes a rule by making it anew under a new id, and pauses none. Answers the rule as it now stands. A sender's placement in Focused or Other is no rule and is not changed here: settings_filters_create with focus moves it, and settings_filters_delete removes it.

from.description: Mail from this sender, or from any of a list of up to 20 email addresses.

query.description: Anything else: a Gmail search query, or for an Outlook mailbox one plain word or quoted phrase in the subject or body, with no AND, OR or NOT in capitals.

subject.description: One plain word or quoted phrase in the subject.

body.description: Outlook only: one plain word or quoted phrase in the body.

to.description: Mail sent to this email address.

toMe.description: Mail sent to the person alone (only, Outlook only), with the person in copy (copy), or either way (either).

size.description: Mail of at least, at most or between these sizes, in kilobytes.

mailingList.description: Outlook only: mail from a mailing list.

importance.description: Outlook only: mail its sender marked at this importance.

addLabelIds.description: Labels to apply, by id. TRASH and SPAM are refused.

removeLabelIds.description: Labels to remove, by id: INBOX takes what the rule matches out of the inbox, UNREAD marks it read.

folder.description: A folder to move what the rule matches into, by its id from labels_list: on an Outlook mailbox never Deleted Items or Junk, or a folder under either; on a Gmail mailbox a label of its own the mail is filed under out of the inbox.

markImportance.description: The importance to give what the rule matches: Outlook's own, or on a Gmail mailbox high marking it important and the others not.

stop.description: Outlook only: true keeps later rules from acting on what this rule matches.

forward.description: Refused: this surface makes no rule that carries mail elsewhere.

enabled.description: Outlook only: false pauses the rule, true resumes it.

tools.name: settings_filters_delete
tools.title: Delete a filter
tools.description: Delete one rule, or one sender's placement in Focused or Other, by its id. Mail it already filed stays where it is.

mailbox.description: The mailbox's name or its email address.

tools.name: settings_send_as_patch
tools.title: Edit the signature
tools.description: Replace the signature of the address the mailbox sends from by default. Nothing of the old one is kept; settings_send_as_get reads it beforehand. An empty signature clears it. Where that address is not the one a Gmail mailbox signs in with, Gmail lets only its own settings change it, and the call is refused. An Outlook mailbox, or one whose provider is imap, keeps no signature a tool reaches, so Lumman keeps this one for it, written as signature or taken with fromDraft from a draft of that mailbox: its formatting, tables and links to web, mail and phone addresses, a picture it links to as that link, and the pictures a draft's signature block holds, at most 10000 bytes once kept, its pictures counted. Written markup keeps a picture only where it names one the kept signature already holds, as cid:<id>. For a mailbox whose provider is imap, displayName sets the name its mail goes out under instead.

mailbox.description: The mailbox's name or its email address.

signature.description: The signature, as HTML. Gmail sanitises it; for an Outlook mailbox, or one whose provider is imap, Lumman keeps what a signature needs of it. Left out where fromDraft or displayName is given.

fromDraft.description: For an Outlook mailbox, or one whose provider is imap: a draft of that mailbox whose signature block - the one its mail app or Lumman marked - is kept with the pictures it holds. Reading it needs messages_get turned on for that mailbox. Left out where signature or displayName is given.

displayName.description: For a mailbox whose provider is imap: the name its mail goes out under beside its address, replacing any taken from its sent mail. Left out where signature or fromDraft is given.

tools.name: settings_send_as_get
tools.title: Read the signature
tools.description: Read the signature of the address the mailbox sends from by default, as HTML, with that address. It goes under the words of every message composed from that address, unless the call passes sign false or the person has said the mailbox's company adds its own on its server. A mailbox with no signature answers without one. For an Outlook mailbox, or one whose provider is imap, it is the one Lumman keeps for it, which settings_send_as_patch sets, naming the pictures it shows without their bytes, beside the name a mailbox whose provider is imap sends under.

mailbox.description: The mailbox's name or its email address.

tools.name: settings_send_as_find
tools.title: Find the signature
tools.description: Find the signature the newest sent mail of an Outlook mailbox, or one whose provider is imap, carries - the block its mail app marked, else the closing lines its messages share, never a line such as Sent from my iPhone - and write it, with its pictures, into a new draft from that mailbox to its own address. That draft is the person's to see, and only on their word does settings_send_as_patch with fromDraft keep the signature from it, before the draft is sent: sent, it is a test message to themselves. It needs messages_get and drafts_create turned on for that mailbox, and is refused while the person has said its company adds a signature on its own server. For a mailbox whose provider is imap it also takes the name its newest sent mail goes out under, where none is held.

mailbox.description: The mailbox's name or its email address.

tools.name: settings_get_vacation
tools.title: Read the vacation responder
tools.description: Read whether a connected mailbox answers mail automatically - an out-of-office or vacation reply - what it says, and any schedule or restriction it carries.

mailbox.description: The mailbox's name or its email address.

tools.name: settings_update_vacation
tools.title: Set the vacation responder
tools.description: Turn the automatic reply - out-of-office, auto-reply or vacation responder - on or off, or change what it says. What this call does not name is kept: its schedule, who it answers, and its words when it is turned off; a schedule it keeps, even one that has ended, still decides when it answers. An Outlook mailbox turned on from off answers from then on, whatever schedule it held, and holds no subject.

mailbox.description: The mailbox's name or its email address.
